from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Diseases spread through population interactions.", 
            "Individuals move between three distinct states.", 
            "Susceptible individuals can become infected.", 
            "Infected individuals eventually recover or gain immunity.", 
            "[Asset: SIR_Flow_Diagram] depicts these dynamic transitions."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: Why do diseases spread?", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Population Cloud
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.08, color=WHITE) for _ in range(20)])
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Just highlighting the states concept, no movement yet
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Patient Zero
        patient_zero = dots[10]
        self.play(patient_zero.animate.set_color("#FF0000"), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5555")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Transmission simulation
        animations = []
        for i in range(len(dots)):
            if i != 10:
                animations.append(dots[i].animate.set_color("#FF5555"))
        self.play(*animations, run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Show SIR Flow Diagram
        # Using a rectangle and text as placeholder for [Asset: SIR_Flow_Diagram]
        sir_diagram = VGroup(
            Rectangle(width=3, height=1.5, color=BLUE),
            Text("S -> I -> R", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(sir_diagram, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(sir_diagram))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Flow: The SIR Engine", [
            "States behave like connected fluid tanks.",
            "Flow rates represent transition speeds.",
            "Contact rates drive Susceptible to Infected.",
            "Recovery rates move Infected to Recovered.",
            "SIR_Tank_Animation illustrates this movement."
        ])

        # Define containers
        s_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        i_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=0.3)
        r_box = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        s_label = Text("S", color="#0000FF").next_to(s_box, UP)
        i_label = Text("I", color="#FF0000").next_to(i_box, UP)
        r_label = Text("R", color="#00FF00").next_to(r_box, UP)

        tanks = VGroup(
            VGroup(s_box, s_label),
            VGroup(i_box, i_label),
            VGroup(r_box, r_label)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        self.place_in_area(tanks, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(tanks)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFB6C1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        # Visual of flow from S to I
        arrow = Arrow(s_box.get_right(), i_box.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF0000")
        # Visual of flow from I to R
        arrow2 = Arrow(i_box.get_right(), r_box.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.wait(1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#90EE90")
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(arrow2))
        
        # Simple simulation of flow
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=s_box.get_center(), color=WHITE) for _ in range(10)])
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.play(dots.animate.move_to(i_box.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.play(dots.animate.move_to(r_box.get_center()), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Reproduction number defines transmission potential.",
            "One person infects several others.",
            "R0_Branching_Tree shows secondary infections."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Pulse: Reproduction Number (R0)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Equation: R0 = beta * c * d
        eq = MathTex(r"R_0 = \beta \cdot c \cdot d", font_size=42, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'C2', 'D5')
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash 'beta' while showing a transmission connection
        beta = eq[0][4]
        self.play(Indicate(beta, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Flash 'c' while showing a network contact diagram
        c_val = eq[0][6]
        self.play(Indicate(c_val, color="#00FFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Represent tree using circles
        tree_nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=0.6, color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[0], 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[1], 'D1')
        self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[2], 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[3], 'D5')
        
        connections = VGroup(
            Line(tree_nodes[0].get_center(), tree_nodes[1].get_center()),
            Line(tree_nodes[0].get_center(), tree_nodes[2].get_center()),
            Line(tree_nodes[0].get_center(), tree_nodes[3].get_center())
        )
        
        self.play(Create(tree_nodes[0]), Create(connections), Create(tree_nodes[1:]))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Simulation & Intervention: Flattening the Curve", 
                          ["Interventions modify transmission parameters.", 
                           "Social distancing reduces contact rates.", 
                           "Visualizing the change."])
        
        # Assets / Graph elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 5, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.6)
        # Placeholder curve 1 (rising infection)
        curve_orig = axes.plot(lambda x: 4 * (x/5) * np.exp(1 - x/5), color=RED)
        # Placeholder curve 2 (flattened)
        curve_flat = axes.plot(lambda x: 2 * (x/5) * np.exp(1 - x/5), color=GREEN)
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve_orig))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        intervention_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 2), axes.c2p(10, 2), color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(intervention_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(curve_orig, curve_flat))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", ["SIR models are predictive tools.", "Parameters guide public health policy.", "Summary_Synthesis_Infographic completes our framework."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'S -> I -> R' model diagram
        s_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=BLUE).add(Text("S", font_size=20))
        i_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=RED).add(Text("I", font_size=20))
        r_node = Circle(radius=0.4, color=GREEN).add(Text("R", font_size=20))
        
        model_group = VGroup(s_node, i_node, r_node).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        arrows = VGroup(
            Arrow(s_node.get_right(), i_node.get_left(), buff=0.1),
            Arrow(i_node.get_right(), r_node.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        )
        sir_diagram = VGroup(model_group, arrows)
        self.place_at_grid(sir_diagram, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(sir_diagram))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash 'R0' above the model, then fade in 'Intervention'
        r0_label = MathTex(r"R_0", color=YELLOW)
        intervention_label = Text("Intervention", color=ORANGE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(r0_label, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(intervention_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(r0_label))
        self.play(Flash(r0_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(intervention_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final screen: 'System Understanding Achieved'
        final_text = Text("System Understanding Achieved", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics

sections.title: The Hook: Why do diseases spread?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of population dynamics using a simple analogy. Establish the three states of an individual: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R).
sections.example: Imagine a 'Z-day' scenario in a high school cafeteria: students who are healthy (S), those who catch a 'zombie-flu' (I), and those who become immune/healed (R).

sections.title: Visualizing the Flow: The SIR Engine
sections.content: Explain the transition rates between states. Introduce the differential equations through visual 'pipes' (S → I → R) where the speed of flow is determined by contact rate (β) and recovery rate (γ).
sections.example: Visualize the population as three connected transparent tanks. The rate at which the 'S' tank drains into the 'I' tank depends on how many 'Zombies' are currently roaming.

sections.title: The Mathematical Pulse: Reproduction Number (R0)
sections.content: Define R0 (R-naught) as the average number of secondary infections caused by one infected individual. Use a graphical tree diagram to show how R0 > 1 leads to exponential growth.
sections.example: Show a character 'Patient Zero' infecting 3 friends (R0=3), then those 3 infecting 9 more, creating a rapidly branching visual tree.

sections.title: Simulation & Intervention: Flattening the Curve
sections.content: Demonstrate how changing parameters (like social distancing) shrinks the 'β' value. Show the movement of the epidemic peak visually using a time-series line graph.
sections.example: Animation of a 'Social Distancing' barrier appearing in the simulation, showing how the 'Infected' curve flattens and stretches over a longer time period.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: SIR models are tools for prediction, not crystal balls. Emphasize that parameters (β and γ) are the levers policymakers use to control outbreaks.
sections.example: A final infographic overlaying a real-world scenario (e.g., vaccine rollout) onto the SIR model curves to show the reduction of the 'Susceptible' pool.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The SIR diagram obstructs the grid visual and lacks focus by being placed too far right in the center of the dot array. Fix: Line 92: self.place_in_area(sir_diagram, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=92, object=sir_diagram)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The dot grid is too large and sparse, leading to inefficient use of the 6x6 workspace. Fix: Line 59: self.place_in_area(dots, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=59, object=dots)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The lecture text is left-aligned but conflicts with the visual space of the grid rows A-C, causing potential clutter. Fix: Line 59: Maintain text position but adjust object grid bounds to 'D1'-'F6' to ensure clear separation. (line=59, object=dots)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The SIR tank animation is positioned too centrally, causing visual clutter and obstructing the logical flow between the lecture text and the right-side elements. Fix: Line 70: self.place_in_area(tanks, 'B4', 'D6', scale_factor=0.55) (line=70, object=tanks)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Labels associated with the S, I, and R boxes lack precise proximity, creating ambiguity regarding which text refers to which fluid tank. Fix: self.place_at_grid(S_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(I_label, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(R_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=71, object=labels)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The animation assets utilize excessive grid space, causing an imbalance between the text area on the left and the functional visual area on the right. Fix: self.place_in_area(SIR_Engine_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5) (line=72, object=SIR_Engine_group)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The branching tree nodes are scattered across rows B and D, causing poor spatial hierarchy and visual clutter. Fix: Line 75-78: self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[0], 'B3', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[1], 'C2', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[2], 'C3', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[3], 'C4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=75, object=tree_nodes)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The equation is centrally placed but occupies an awkward horizontal span, competing with the tree visualization. Fix: Line 58: self.place_in_area(eq, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8) (line=58, object=eq)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The branching tree visualization is too wide, potentially encroaching on the left-side lecture text area. Fix: Line 75-78: Scale down node group and constrain to 'B4' to 'D6' sub-grid to maintain clearance from text. (line=75, object=tree_nodes)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The graph's origin and labels are too close to the left-side text, causing visual crowding and potential obstruction of the lecture notes. Fix: self.place_in_area(axes, 'C2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=59, object=axes)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The curve visual occupies too much vertical space, potentially clipping if the window is resized or if labels are added. Fix: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=0.75) (line=59, object=axes)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Poor utilization of the right-hand grid space; the graph is currently centered too far left, competing with the text block. Fix: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.85) (line=59, object=axes)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The sir_diagram is positioned too far left, creating visual clutter near the lecture text. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(sir_diagram, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=61, object=sir_diagram)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The r0_label overlaps with the top boundary of the diagram; scale is inconsistent. Fix: Line 70: self.place_at_grid(r0_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=70, object=r0_label)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The 'System Understanding Achieved' text is placed too low, encroaching on the F row. Fix: Line 81: self.place_in_area(final_text, 'E2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9) (line=81, object=final_text)

The SIR diagram obstructs the grid visual and lacks focus by being placed too far right in the center of the dot array. Please update positioning as per suggestion: self.place_in_area(sir_diagram, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6). Also, please adjust the dot grid (self.place_in_area(dots, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.5)) to improve workspace usage and prevent conflict with lecture text.

The SIR tank animation is positioned too centrally, causing visual clutter. Please update: self.place_in_area(tanks, 'B4', 'D6', scale_factor=0.55). Adjust label proximity: self.place_at_grid(S_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(I_label, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(R_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7). Finally, constrain SIR_Engine_group: self.place_in_area(SIR_Engine_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.5).

The branching tree nodes are scattered and the equation occupies awkward space. Please update node placement: self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[0], 'B3', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[1], 'C2', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[2], 'C3', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(tree_nodes[3], 'C4', scale_factor=0.6). Update equation: self.place_in_area(eq, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8). Ensure tree visualization is constrained to B4-D6 sub-grid.

The graph axes and curve need better placement to avoid crowding the lecture text and to improve grid utilization. Please update: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.85). Also, ensure that the curve visual is adjusted so it does not clip.

The sir_diagram is positioned too far left; move to: self.place_at_grid(sir_diagram, 'C3', scale_factor=0.7). Adjust r0_label: self.place_at_grid(r0_label, 'B3', scale_factor=0.9). Fix final_text positioning: self.place_in_area(final_text, 'E2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.9).
